results.title: The quadratic field $\mathbb Q(\sqrt d)$
results.caption: Definition
results.lean: ZInQ.Progressions.Qsqrt, ZInQ.Progressions.Qsqrt.instNumberField, ZInQ.Progressions.Qsqrt.instCharZero, ZInQ.Progressions.Qsqrt.finrank, ZInQ.Progressions.Qsqrt.not_isSquare_of_squarefree, ZInQ.Progressions.Qsqrt.fact_not_isSquare, ZInQ.Progressions.Qsqrt.sqrtInt, ZInQ.Progressions.Qsqrt.sqrtInt_sq
results.summary: For an integer $d$, let $K_d=\mathbb Q(\sqrt d)=\mathbb Q[X]/(X^2-d)$ be the $\mathbb Q$-algebra with basis $1,\sqrt d$ and $(\sqrt d)^2=d$. If $d$ is not the square of a rational number, then $K_d$ is a number field of degree $[K_d:\mathbb Q]=2$, and $\sqrt d$ is an algebraic integer of $K_d$ with square $d$. Every squarefree integer $d\ne1$ satisfies this hypothesis.

results.title: The signature of $\mathbb Q(\sqrt d)$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $d$ be an integer that is not the square of a rational number and $K=\mathbb Q(\sqrt d)$, with $r_1$ real and $r_2$ complex places. If $d<0$, then $r_1=0$ and $r_2=1$, and $K$ is totally complex; if $d>0$, then $r_1=2$ and $r_2=0$, and $K$ is totally real.

results.title: Roots of unity in a quadratic field
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ be a number field of degree $2$, for example $K=\mathbb Q(\sqrt d)$ with $d$ an integer that is not the square of a rational number. The group of roots of unity of $K$ has order $w_K\le6$.

results.title: The regulator of an imaginary quadratic field
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $d<0$ be an integer (so $d$ is not the square of a rational number) and $K=\mathbb Q(\sqrt d)$. Then the regulator of $K$ is $R_K=1$.
